summary:
## Background
Thiopurines (azathioprine, mercaptopurine, thioguanine) are widely used in IBD, hematologic malignancies, and autoimmune diseases but can cause severe toxicity. This case report describes a South Asian woman who developed profound myelosuppression, hepatotoxicity, and alopecia after mercaptopurine; she had wildtype TPMT but was homozygous for NUDT15*3 (c.415C>T, R139C), indicating complete NUDT15 loss of function.

## Key Findings
- NUDT15 deficiency:
  - Homozygous NUDT15*3/*3 markedly increases thiopurine intolerance. In the literature, NUDT15*3 homozygotes tolerated only ~8% of the standard mercaptopurine dose before significant toxicity, similar to TPMT poor metabolizers.
  - NUDT15 loss-of-function alleles are more frequent in Asians and Hispanics: approximately 21% carry one LOF allele and ~2% carry two, versus ~10% and 0.3% for TPMT LOF in Europeans/Africans, respectively, indicating higher testing yield in these groups.
- TPMT deficiency:
  - TPMT variants (*2, *3A, *3C, *3B) explain the majority of decreased-function phenotypes; individuals with two LOF alleles (poor metabolizers) almost universally develop severe toxicity even with ~10-fold dose reductions.
  - A randomized study in IBD showed pretreatment TPMT genotyping with dose adjustment reduced hematologic adverse events ~10-fold in at-risk patients.
- Clinical phenotype signal:
  - Alopecia can be an early manifestation of thiopurine toxicity and may precede cytopenias; while characteristic in NUDT15 deficiency, it can occur without NUDT15 variants as well.

## Clinical Implications
- Genotype both NUDT15 and TPMT before initiating thiopurines, especially in Asian and Hispanic patients where NUDT15 variants are common; relying on TPMT alone may miss high-risk patients.
- For NUDT15 poor metabolizers (e.g., NUDT15*3/*3), avoid thiopurines or consider only very low doses with intensive monitoring; severe toxicity can occur even with large dose reductions (case drug was discontinued).
- For any patient on thiopurines, monitor closely for early alopecia and cytopenias; prompt drug cessation and pharmacogenetic testing are warranted if these occur.
- Incorporating NUDT15 alongside TPMT testing can improve safety by guiding dosing, selecting alternatives, and reducing serious hematologic events.
